kevin: Heads-up — noticed a regression in streaming RPC P95. Host-side overhead jumped ~20-40% after the framer change (rolling 2 weeks). Traces point to tokenization + framer scheduling.
anya: ugh. which framer change? the windowed coalescer we landed last week?
kevin: yes. the allocator path in the new coalescer appears to force small memcpy rounds for every chunk. p95 increased on ~1k token streams.
sam: can you paste the flame? also which client (http2/gRPC)?
kevin: gRPC streaming (HTTP2). attaching quick flame excerpt below from perf script:
```
  45.2%  runtime_host  host_framer::coalesce
  22.1%  runtime_host  tokenize::utf8_scan
   8.9%  libc          memcpy
   6.5%  runtime_host  ingress_parser::parse_headers
   4.7%  kernel       epoll_wait
```
irene: memcpy being hot implies small, repeated buffers. Did the coalescer stop using iovecs/writev?
kevin: yep. we switched to a contiguous buffer for a 'simpler' decoder; that causes repeated grow/copy for fragmented client streams.
perf-bot: PERF ALERT: host_stream_p95 increased from 12.4ms -> 16.9ms over last deploy. Top callsites: coalesce(), utf8_scan(), memcpy().
anya: quick idea: try falling back to writev path and keep prefix caching. can we toggle via feature flag?
sam: I ran an A/B locally: enabling writev reduces memcpy by ~60% and drops tokenization stall spikes. Command I used:
```
RUNTIME_FRAMER=writev ./bazel run //runtime:server -- --ingress-framer=writev
perf record -g -o /tmp/perf.dat ./stress_stream 1000
perf script /tmp/perf.dat | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg
```
kevin: nice. also noticed UTF8 scanner re-scans same buffer when framing splits across chunk boundary. we can track partial state across framer boundaries to avoid re-parse.
irene: that's the KV cache interact: when prefix cache hits, we still tokenize from chunk start because framer reassembles. If framer exposes fragment metadata we can skip.
anya: can someone prototype a framer flag that preserves iovecs + exposes fragment offsets? low-risk revert if it fails.
sam: ill make a tiny patch to re-enable iovecs and add fragment metadata on the wire. will run perf tests after lunch.
kevin: also postmortem note: we should add a unit perf test that simulates 8-16 small frames per request to catch this in CI.
perf-bot: TODO added: ENG-RUNTIME-457: add small-fragment streaming perf job to CI (assigned: sam).
kevin: thanks. if anyone has quick microbench numbers, drop them here. goal: get p95 back under 13ms by EOD next sprint.
anya: will follow up with a short RFC describing framer options and expected tradeoffs. :thumbsup!
